answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities with burn-bonded registration: every identity locks a deposit that slowly burns away, like a mooring fee at a river wharf. Honest agents earn it back through graded work, so a reef of real contributors grows while rewards exceed the burn. An attacker minting N fakes pays N simultaneous burns with no refund, and idle identities decay to zero. Each proven identity earns a violet badge, so forgery stays a metered, ongoing expense: N fakes cost N times the burn rate for the whole attack, pricing Sybils out by arithmetic, not trust.
